said:
Remaining pallet space is obtained from the capacity and stock figures, adding the Omsk annex that the capacity return omitted.  
Kirov: 4000 − 3100 = 900.  
Omsk: 2500 + 1200 − 1900 = 1800.  
Tara: 3000 − 2000 = 1000.  
Kirov therefore has the smallest unused capacity and is the first to run out.  
ANSWER: kirov

The annex must be added to Omsk’s as-built figure, giving current capacities of 4000 / 3700 / 3000. Remaining headroom on Monday is therefore 900 / 1800 / 1000 pallets. Dividing by the recorded weekly net intakes yields 3.0 / 7.2 / 3.85 weeks, so Kirov reaches capacity first. (The rail-strike note confirms the stock figures already include the delayed Tara loads; the extra Kirov shift is already reflected in the averaged intake.)

ANSWER: kirov

The given capacities are as-built figures. The Omsk annex (handed over in March) is additional usable space, so Omsk’s true capacity is 3 700 pallets. Remaining head-room on Monday is therefore:

- Kirov 900 pallets,
- Omsk 1 800 pallets,
- Tara 1 000 pallets.

Dividing by the recorded net weekly intakes yields 3 weeks, 7.2 weeks and ≈3.85 weeks respectively. Kirov therefore reaches capacity first. (The rail-strike note is already reflected in the stock figures and does not alter the arithmetic.)

ANSWER: kirov

Kirov remaining space is 4000 - 3100 = 900 pallets at 300/week (3 weeks).  
Omsk remaining space (including annex) is 3700 - 1900 = 1800 pallets at 250/week (7.2 weeks).  
Tara remaining space is 3000 - 2000 = 1000 pallets at 260/week (~3.85 weeks).  
Kirov therefore reaches capacity first.

ANSWER: kirov
